clue.text: Lead free paint, put on crusaders' armour originally

indicators.note: what something was originally is how it began, so only the starting letters of these words count
letters set free are released from their order and can fall into a new arrangement
in an across clue, something put on another is placed after it, so the shuffled part follows

blocks.note: the opening letters of these two words
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A decorator is told to use lead-free paint on a suit of Crusader armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead free' reads as one phrase about safe paint; split it, and 'Lead' is a verb meaning to head a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To captain a side or crew is to be in charge of it, so the verb is a synonym of command.

clue.text: Dramatist's restraint beginning to deteriorate in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

blocks.note: a check is a curb or restraint
food that is going off is starting to spoil

explanation.surface: A playwright's self-control starts to slip during a casting session.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, 'check off' sounds like the Russian writer's name. 'Audition' fits the theatre picture but works as the hearing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov was the Russian author of The Seagull and The Cherry Orchard, a playwright.

clue.text: Widespread alarm about or before noon

indicators.note: one thing about another goes round it, so the alarm word encloses the rest

blocks.note: panic is sudden alarm
taken as written
a.m. marks the hours before midday

explanation.surface: Fear spreads widely through a town some time in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before noon' is the abbreviation printed on clocks and timetables for morning hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view takes in a wide sweep of scenery, so it is broad or widespread in extent.

clue.text: Law centre provided with elements of a good defence

indicators.note: the centre of a three-letter word is its single middle letter

blocks.note: the middle letter of this word
two chemical elements: Li is lithium and Bi is bismuth

explanation.surface: A legal advice office supplies the basics of a sound case for the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elements' sounds like basic parts of an argument, but here it means chemical symbols from the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is proof of being elsewhere when a crime happened, about the strongest answer an accused person can offer.

clue.text: New expression in some lingo, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words are only one possible version, so their letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A freshly coined phrase turns up in a slang or jargon of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined word or phrase, from Greek roots meaning new and word.

clue.text: Slander, for instance, by verbal contract

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the next word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: as in 'cities, as London' means for instance
to purse the lips is to contract or pucker them

explanation.surface: Defamation is given as an example of something agreed only by word of mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verbal contract' looks like one legal phrase; split it, 'verbal' is the sound signal and 'contract' is the verb to tighten.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse someone is to spread damaging falsehoods about them, an old verb with the sense to defame or slander.

clue.text: Trap half concealed pest

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is two of its letters, here the back pair

blocks.note: the second half of this word
hid is the past tense of hide, to conceal

explanation.surface: A snare lies partly hidden to catch some vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are greenfly and blackfly, tiny sap-sucking insects that gardeners treat as a nuisance to plants.

clue.text: Run record held by contemporary player

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

blocks.note: a peer is someone of the same age or standing
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
a person's form is their track record, as a criminal record or form book

explanation.surface: A modern sportsman holds a record for running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run record' reads as one athletic feat, but the two words are separate pieces, both held inside the word for a contemporary.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor or musician is a player, someone who performs before an audience, so a performer.

clue.text: Soldiers get about an hour in the river

indicators.note: to get about something is to surround it, so the soldiers wrap round the rest

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
h is the standard abbreviation for hour
taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops spend some sixty minutes swimming in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' does double work: it is both a piece inside RE and the joining word to the definition, so only one 'in' is used as a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European waterway flowing from the Swiss Alps to the North Sea.

clue.text: Opponents outflanking many equally balanced sides

indicators.note: troops outflanking an enemy get round both its sides, so these letters go either side of the rest

blocks.note: East and South are opposing partnerships at the bridge table
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
even scales are level, in balance

explanation.surface: Two well-matched teams face rivals who get round their flanks.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play against East and West, so any one of N or S with E or W makes a pair of opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket and football teams have eleven players, so a side is often called an eleven.

clue.text: Boredom leads to emotional numbness — never using imagination

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front letters, so only the opening of each word counts

blocks.note: the initial letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Tedium brings on a dulled feeling and a mind that never invents anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui, borrowed from French, is listless weariness from having nothing interesting to do.

clue.text: White rose displayed in a different way

indicators.note: flowers displayed are arranged for show, so the letters are set out in a new order

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A white bloom is arranged unusually in a flower show.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise as an adverb means differently, by other means, as in 'he thinks otherwise'.

clue.text: Daring novelist read aloud to poet

indicators.note: reading aloud gives the sound of the name, not its spelling

blocks.note: Thomas Hardy wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles
Thomas Hood was a Victorian comic poet

explanation.surface: A bold author reads his work aloud to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Both writers are named Thomas; the sound signal applies to the novelist only, whose spelling HARDY becomes HARDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardihood is boldness or audacity, the quality of being hardy and brave, so daring as a noun.

clue.text: Award to leaders of Shakespearian England — like Falstaff, perhaps

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so only the opening letters of the following words count

blocks.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
the first letters of these words

explanation.surface: An honour goes to leading Elizabethan figures, among them Shakespeare's fat knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff in Henry IV is famously fat, a corpulent knight given to drink and food.

clue.text: Improvises repairs

blocks.note: first meaning: a musician ... by improvising a simple repeated accompaniment
second meaning: to vamp up old shoes or clothes is to patch them

explanation.surface: Someone makes do with makeshift mending.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both playing an extemporised accompaniment and patching up something old, the vamp being a shoe's upper.

clue.text: Suddenly cheerful although punch-drunk

blocks.note: slap as an adverb means abruptly, as in 'slap in the middle'
a synonym

explanation.surface: Someone becomes abruptly cheery despite being dazed from blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Although' is an unusual joining word, setting the two halves against the definition as if in contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-happy first described a boxer dazed and giddy from too many blows, which is what punch-drunk means.

clue.text: Hints to close friends

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, suggests indirectly
second meaning: as a noun, people one is very familiar with

explanation.surface: Someone passes tips on to their inner circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are said differently: the verb ends like 'mates', the noun like 'mitts'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make known indirectly, while the plural noun means people bound by close personal ties.

clue.text: Concentric blooms found in house-plant

blocks.note: the House of Tudor was the English royal dynasty of Henry VIII
a familiar flowering shrub

explanation.surface: Ring-shaped flowers are spotted on a potted indoor specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House-plant' looks like a single word for an indoor pot plant; the hyphen hides a royal house followed by a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic emblem of England sets a white rose inside a red one, two flowers one within the other.

clue.text: Things for sale under the counter in China

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word under another is written below it, so it comes second

blocks.note: a table is a flat counter or surface
ware means goods offered for sale

explanation.surface: Black-market goods are sold illicitly in the People's Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the counter' is an idiom for illicit trade, and 'China' with its capital letter looks like the country.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain for plates and cups, the crockery set out for meals.

clue.text: Popular current demand by journalist

blocks.note: AC is alternating current
to claim something is to demand it as one's right
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Popular power trends are demanded by a newspaper writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaimed means widely praised and applauded, so well liked by the public.

clue.text: Perversely creating a stymie

blocks.note: taken as written
to stymie a plan is to block or frustrate it

explanation.surface: Someone awkwardly sets up an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart means across or in opposition to, so it can mean contrary to what is wanted or expected.

clue.text: Defeat drunken brute

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone overpowers a sozzled thug.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut an argument is to disprove it, and in older use to drive back an attack, beating it.

clue.text: Score century without one attempt to cheat!

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so these letters wrap round the next piece

blocks.note: a try is a score in rugby
I is the Roman numeral for one
a ton is a hundred, as in a hundred runs in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman scores a hundred alone, and it looks like foul play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like an instruction to remove the one; in its archaic sense of outside, the score and the century go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To try it on is a British idiom for testing how far you can go with a cheeky deception.

clue.text: Yank in difficulty.. .

blocks.note: first meaning: to ... up trousers is to jerk them upward
second meaning: a snag or temporary problem

explanation.surface: An American finds himself in trouble, with the story continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' with a capital looks like an American; it is the verb to pull. The trailing dots link this surface to the next clue's.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to pull sharply upward, and the noun names an obstacle that holds things up.

clue.text: Unqualified youngster - a beginner

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
taken as written
L is for learner, from the plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A young novice has no qualifications at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unqualified' suggests lacking a certificate, but here it means absolute, as in unqualified success.
explanation.definitionFit: Total in the sense of complete or absolute matches unqualified meaning without reservation or limit.

clue.text: ... appropriately, in foreign city

blocks.note: German is one example of foreign
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, an American has trouble fittingly, in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots join this to 21 across for the surface reading only; the wordplay stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant or pertinent, so germanely means in a fitting, relevant manner.

clue.text: Soldiers take a very short time to make this gadget

blocks.note: GIs are American soldiers
a mo is a moment

explanation.surface: Troops need only a moment to build a device.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo, also spelt gizmo, is a slang word for any small gadget or device.

clue.text: Get together for a service

blocks.note: taken as written
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A congregation gathers for worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get together' reads as people meeting; it means to accumulate things.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or collect a large quantity, so to bring things together.

clue.text: Endless noise at tap dancing course

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the word loses its final letter
dancers move about and change places, so the letters do too

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Constant clatter from tap dancers during a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tap dancing' reads as one activity and 'course' as a class; 'dancing' is the shuffle signal and 'course' is part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter of cold meats and vegetables, the first course of a meal.

clue.text: A vehicle turning to one side

indicators.note: a vehicle turning round heads back the way it came, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A car swerves off to the side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart can mean aside or separately, as in a joke said apart or standing apart from a group.

clue.text: Encouragement to pack, even if receiving a friend

indicators.note: a word receiving another takes it inside itself

blocks.note: tho is an informal spelling of though, meaning even if
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to pack a suitcase, even while a friend is visiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' suggests packing bags; it is a pack of hounds, which the hunting cry spurs on when the fox is sighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the huntsman's shout on spotting the fox, urging the hounds and riders onward.

clue.text: Festival new in the Orient

blocks.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fresh celebration takes place in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient means the East, so something found there is eastern, of or in that region.
